deep.reconstruction:
This is page 1 (marked [C] ①) of an 'old draft' for the spring-1981 work, which became the Teichmüller tower / Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The margin heading reads roughly '+ structure d'extension de Σ = Σ_{0,3}'. The page studies outer automorphisms of the profinite 'groupe à lacets' Π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}). Here 'lacets' means loops with the peripheral (inertia) structure.

Step 1: the presentation. Take generators l_0, l_1, l_∞ subject to l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1, so the group is free profinite on l_0, l_1.

Step 2: endomorphisms. An endomorphism is given by any triple (l'_0, l'_1, l'_∞) satisfying the same relation. It is an automorphism if the triple topologically generates the group, by the Hopfian property of finitely generated profinite groups.

Step 3: the cyclic automorphism. Define ρ by l_0 ↦ l_1 ↦ l_∞ ↦ l_0. It respects the relation, since l_1 l_∞ l_0 is a conjugate of 1, and ρ^3 = id.

Step 4: the transposition. Define σ_∞ by:
- l_0 ↔ l_1,
- l_∞ ↦ (l_1 l_0)^{-1} = l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1}.
This equals l_0^{-1} l_∞ l_0, a conjugate of l_∞, so σ_∞ respects the 'local structure' with multiplier (cyclotomic-type character) 1. Also σ_∞^2 = id. Define σ_0 and σ_1 by transport of structure, ρ σ_i ρ^{-1} = σ_{ρ(i)}.

Step 5: the problem posed. The aim is to make S_3 = Sym{0,1,∞} act on π while respecting inertia classes. The cyclic subgroup S_3^+ ≅ Z/3 does act genuinely.

Step 6: the continuation (next page). There one finds σ_0σ_1 = int(l_1^{-1})ρ. So S_3 acts only on the outer group. Grothendieck explains this geometrically:
- S_3 has no common fixed point on P^1 − {0,1,∞};
- ρ does have fixed points (the primitive sixth roots of unity, which he writes ±j), which can serve as base point.

In modern terms, this is the extension 1 → π_{0,3} → π_1^orb([(P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3]) → S_3 → 1. Discretely this is 1 → Γ(2)/±1 → PSL_2(Z) → S_3 → 1, and its profinite completion is the 'structure d'extension' of the margin note. This is groundwork for describing Γ̂_{0,3} (the extended Teichmüller group, including complex conjugation) acting on π̂_{0,3}. It is also groundwork for the relations later encoded in the GT definition (the θ and ω relations of Drinfeld/Ihara).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The formula σ_∞(l_∞) = (l_1 l_0)^{-1} = l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1} is correct, and it equals l_0^{-1} l_∞ l_0. The garbled parenthetical should read (= l_0^{-1} l_∞ l_0).
Minor: 'si fermés' is a doubtful reading. The intended point is simply that topological generation suffices for an automorphism (Hopfian property).
Next page: S_3 does have fixed points on P^1 − {0,1,∞}: −1, 1/2 and 2 for the transpositions, and e^{±iπ/3} for ρ. What it lacks is a common fixed point, which is what Grothendieck means.

ideas.what: Presentation of π̂_{0,3} with three inertia generators l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. Endomorphisms are given by triples satisfying the relation, and are automorphisms iff the triple topologically generates.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞} with peripheral structure; Hopfian property of finitely generated profinite groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (SGA1 for the profinite π_1; Belyi/Ihara for the arithmetic framing)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (structure of π_1); Esquisse d'un programme (π_{0,3} and the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Cyclic automorphism ρ and transpositions σ_i of π_{0,3} preserving inertia classes with multiplier 1, with ρσ_iρ^{-1} = σ_{ρ(i)}.
ideas.modern_name: S_3 outer action on F̂_2 (the anharmonic group action on the λ-line); θ and ω automorphisms in Drinfeld's/Ihara's definition of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for the discrete case (PSL_2(Z) ⊃ Γ(2)); profinite/GT framing Drinfeld 1990, Ihara 1990–91, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to Γ_{0,3} and the S_3 symmetry, but these explicit formulas are not published there

ideas.what: Extension structure 1 → π_{0,3} → ? → S_3 → 1, with only an outer action of S_3 but a genuine action of Z/3 because ρ has a fixed point (used as base point).
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of M_{0,3}/S_3 ≅ PSL_2(Z) (profinitely completed); extended Teichmüller group Γ̂_{0,[3]}

deep.surprise_reason: These are early working notes setting up the S_3 symmetry of π̂_{0,3}. The content is classical (PSL_2(Z) as an extension of S_3 by Γ(2)) and was later fully absorbed into the GT literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps). It is historically nice as a 1981 precursor of the θ/ω relations, but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The parenthetical after σ_∞(l_∞) should read '(= l_0^{-1} l_∞ l_0)', i.e. a conjugate of l_∞, not '(=l_0^{-1}(l_0^{-1}).l_∞)'.
The insertion '(échangeant l_1 et l_0 resp. l_∞ et l_0)' should be '(échangeant l_1 et l_∞ resp. l_∞ et l_0)', referring to σ_0 and σ_1 respectively, consistent with ρσ_iρ^{-1} = σ_{ρ(i)}.
'Un endomorphisme de Π_{0,3}': the image has a hatted/abbreviated Π_{0,3}.
Margin: '+ structure d'extension de Σ = Σ_{0,3}' (the left-margin annotation), plus a stray '4' (archive page number) at the bottom left.
